content.comment_body: I purchased [product_name] [version_no] (Single Licence) and installed it on my desktop running Windows XP, where I develop programs. Everything works well there. I then installed it on my laptop (also XP) for accessing [product_name] at client sites. The only way to prevent [product_name] from freezing on the laptop is to keep the installation CD in the drive. Does this mean I need to purchase an additional [version_no] licence for my laptop?
Closed because the question was posted twice. The second thread with this topic is available in the [product_name] conference. Best regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user reports that [product_name] [version_no] freezes on a laptop running Windows XP unless the installation CD remains in the drive. This limits mobility and usability, especially for fieldwork, and raises concerns about software licensing and legacy protection mechanisms impacting workflow.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects [product_name] to operate independently after installation without needing the CD, especially for portable use, and requests clarification regarding licensing for multiple devices.
